grammarPoint.title: Future continuous
grammarPoint.summary: Use the future continuous to talk about actions that will be in progress at a specific time or over a period in the future.
grammarPoint.explanation:
The future continuous describes an action that will be ongoing at a particular moment or over a period in the future. It emphasizes the duration of the action rather than its completion.

We often use it to set the scene for another future event, or to talk about something that will be happening when something else occurs. It can also be used to ask politely about someone's future plans.

Think of it as looking back from a point in the future and seeing an action in progress. For example, "This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Rome" means that at that exact moment, the action of flying will be happening.
patterns: Subject + will not be + verb-ing (won't be)

examples.text: This time next week, I'll be relaxing on the beach.
examples.note: Describes an action that will be in progress at a specific future time.

examples.text: They won't be attending the meeting tomorrow morning.
examples.note: Shows an action that will not be ongoing in the future.

examples.text: Will you be working late tonight?
examples.note: Asks about an ongoing activity or plan in the future.

examples.text: When you call, I'll probably be cooking dinner.
examples.note: Indicates an action that will be in progress when another future event happens.

examples.text: By 5 PM, she will be finishing her presentation.
examples.note: Refers to an action that will be ongoing up to or at a specific future point.

commonErrors.wrong: Tomorrow at 3 PM, I will work.
commonErrors.right: Tomorrow at 3 PM, I will be working.
commonErrors.note: Use future continuous for an action ongoing at a specific future time.

commonErrors.wrong: When you arrive, I will cook.
commonErrors.right: When you arrive, I will be cooking.
commonErrors.note: Use future continuous for an action in progress when another event happens.

commonErrors.wrong: She won't be finish her report by Friday.
commonErrors.right: She won't be finishing her report by Friday.
commonErrors.note: Remember to use the -ing form after 'be'.

exercises.question: Don't call me at 7 PM. I ___ dinner with my family.
exercises.explanation: The future continuous describes an action that will be in progress at a specific future time.

exercises.question: By this time next year, she ___ her master's degree.
exercises.explanation: The future continuous shows an action that will be ongoing over a period leading up to or at a future point.

exercises.question: What ___ when the guests arrive?
exercises.explanation: Use the future continuous to ask about an action that will be in progress at a future moment.

exercises.question: I can't meet you on Saturday morning. I ___ the garden.
exercises.explanation: The future continuous indicates an activity that will be ongoing at a specific future time.

exercises.text: This evening, I ___ (read) a new novel.
exercises.explanation: The future continuous shows an action in progress at a specific time in the future.

exercises.text: They ___ (not / wait) for us when we get there.
exercises.explanation: Use the negative future continuous to describe an action that will not be in progress.
The future continuous is used to ask about ongoing actions in the future.

answers: I will be watching a movie at 9 PM.

answers: Will you be working on Saturday?
